name: Adductor-Related Groin Pain
summary: Groin pain associated with the adductor muscle-tendon complex, often provoked by resisted adduction and palpation near the adductor origin.

looksLike: Pain with squeezing, sprinting or kicking
Symptoms after rapid change of direction
redFlags: Acute testicular pain/swelling or abdominal emergency
Trauma with inability to weight bear
firstSteps: Reduce painful sprinting, kicking and cutting load
Maintain pain-tolerable walking and hip ROM

tests.name: Resisted Adduction Squeeze Test
tests.purpose: Assess adductor-related symptom reproduction and baseline capacity.
tests.positive: Familiar groin pain during resisted adduction.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Reduce painful sprinting, kicking and cutting load
Maintain pain-tolerable walking and hip ROM
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
do: Progress adductor strength through short to long muscle lengths
Add trunk, hip and lower-limb strength
Restore linear running before high-speed cutting
dose: Copenhagen progression at suitable lever: 2–3 x 6–12
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Progress sprinting, kicking and multidirectional drills
dose: Progress total weekly field exposure gradually
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: Adductor strength and squeeze tolerance restored
Sprint, kick and cutting tasks completed at high intensity
Full training exposure without significant next-day flare

structures: Adductor longus and adjacent adductor muscle-tendon complex
Pubic aponeurosis may coexist in athletic groin pain
mechanism: Cutting, kicking or rapid direction change
Sudden increase in sprinting or adductor loading
classification: Adductor-related; assess coexisting iliopsoas, inguinal, pubic or hip-related causes using Doha framework
investigations: Clinical classification first; MRI/ultrasound for persistent uncertainty, suspected tear or stress injury.
Urgent medical assessment for testicular, abdominal or fracture red flags.
manual: Manual therapy may address associated hip mobility restriction but is not a substitute for adductor loading.
modalities: No modality replaces progressive adductor strength and sport exposure.
Compression shorts may be comfortable but are not a treatment by themselves.
mistakes: Returning when straight-line jogging is pain-free but cutting remains painful
Ignoring hip joint or stress-fracture differential
pearls: Use the Doha classification to describe the clinical entity, not to assume a single tissue diagnosis.
Copenhagen exercise should be progressed to current capacity.

tests.name: Resisted Adduction Squeeze Test
tests.purpose: Assess adductor-related symptom reproduction and baseline capacity.
tests.positive: Familiar groin pain during resisted adduction.
tests.patientPosition: Supine with hips flexed to a comfortable standard angle; place dynamometer or ball between knees and request graded squeeze.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Supports adductor-related groin pain; use palpation and Doha differential classification.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
